LESSON: LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 5.1.1: Listening Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly
2. use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly
3. listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication
4. respond to information from an oral text

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING COMPREHENSION
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening Comprehension helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Respond to information from an oral text

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to information from an oral text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to information from an oral text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to information from an oral text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening Comprehension to a partner. (skill: use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Listening Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond to information from an oral text)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly.
3. Practise this skill: use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly.
4. Practise this skill: listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Listening Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly?
2. How can we improve our pronunciation?
3. Why should we listen attentively?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly.
5. Be able to: use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
